subject: Private Offer: annual prepay + ramp schedule — proposed amendment
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.inference.com>
To: Alicia Gomez <agomez@acme-retail.com>
Cc: 
Date: Sun, 07 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Private Offer: annual prepay + ramp schedule — initial proposal

Hi Alicia,

Thanks for the time yesterday. Per our conversation I’m sending a concise proposal for an AWS Private Offer that matches Acme’s procurement cadence while keeping unit economics predictable for you. High level: 12-month annual prepay with a structured ramp (month-by-month consumption credit schedule) and a term discount that increases with committed spend.

Proposal (summary):
- Term: 12 months, annual prepay (paid up front via AWS private offer)
- Commitment: $600k annual committed spend (prepay)
- Ramp schedule (consumption credits): month 1 = 40% of committed tokens available, month 2 = 60%, month 3+ = 100%
- Discount: 18% off list for first year; additional 2% unlock at 18 mos touching if you convert to 24-month commit at renewal (we can add a mid-term true-up)
- Marketplace flow: AWS private offer with PO from Acme, Redwood invoices per the private offer terms for usage swallow/true-up if consumption exceeds prepay in the year

Attachments: Redwood_PrivateOffer_Acme_2026_v1.pdf (offer summary + SKU breakdown).

If this is directionally acceptable I’ll loop in RevOps and Legal to produce a redline-friendly offer and get an AWS private-offer link generated. Two quick questions for your procurement team so we can finalize the invoice cadence and termination language:
1) Does Acme require a revenue guarantee minimum beyond the prepay (we typically avoid minimums beyond the committed prepay amount)?
2) Any required contract language for data residency or additional SOC artifacts beyond SOC2 Type II?

Goal: get a signed private offer + payment before end of November to hit provisioning windows and reserved capacity.

Regards,
Sergio
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Redwood_PrivateOffer_Acme_2026_v1.pdf (pdf, 220 KB)]

From: Alicia Gomez <agomez@acme-retail.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Ben Turner <b.turner@acme-retail.com>
Date: Sun, 07 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private Offer: annual prepay + ramp schedule — initial proposal

Sergio — thanks, this looks close to what Procurement wants. A couple of constraints from our side:

- We can do an annual prepay but our preferred accounting requires the invoice be dated for the start of the fiscal quarter (we’re Q4 close Nov 30).
- We can’t accept consumption cliffs that block us operationally — month 1 at 40% might be challenging for us. If the ramp is there for budget reasons we’d need a temporary overage allowance or a smoother ramp.
- Legal will ask to cap the vendor liability and include a 30-day termination for convenience with pro-rata refund for unused prepay beyond a small admin fee.

I’ve looped in Ben (procurement) for the PO timing. Can you share a 2nd option with either a smoother ramp or a 24-month commit alternative? Also need to confirm SOC2 + penetration test report availability.

—Alicia
Alicia Gomez
Head of Cloud Procurement, Acme Retail
[signature redacted]

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.inference.com>
To: Alicia Gomez <agomez@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Ben Turner <b.turner@acme-retail.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Sun, 07 Nov 2026 13:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private Offer: annual prepay + ramp schedule — initial proposal

Thanks Alicia — helpful context. Quick answers and two revised options below. We have SOC2 Type II + recent pen test available; I’ll attach the SOC2 pointer in the next note.

Option A — 12-month (smoother ramp + small overage buffer):
- Commitment: $600k annual prepay (same)
- Ramp: month 1 = 60%, month 2 = 80%, month 3+ = 100%
- Overages: up to 10% monthly overage allowed without immediate true-up; single true-up at quarter boundary
- Discount: 16% off list (we reduce a bit to support smoother ramp and overage buffer)

Option B — 24-month (deep discount for multi-year commit):
- Commitment: $1.08M committed over 24 months (equivalent to $540k/yr)
- Ramp: immediate 100% availability month 1 (since longer-term commitment)
- Discount: 22% off list, with an annual pricing floor to protect both parties

Legal note: we can accommodate a 30-day termination for convenience but need a short admin fee (1% of remaining prepay) to cover reserved capacity reallocation and provisioning costs. We’ll propose language in the private-offer redline.

Next steps: confirmation of preferred option + PO timing. If you pick Option A we can generate the AWS private-offer for signature this week and ship the invoice to hit your fiscal quarter.

Sergio
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Redwood_PrivateOffer_Acme_2026_v1.pdf (updated)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Mon, 08 Nov 2026 09:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private Offer: annual prepay + ramp schedule — initial proposal

Sergio — copied Marissa (RevOps). Quick commercial read: Option A is fine but suggest the following tweaks to reduce billing friction and make it procurement-friendly:

- Make invoice dated to the first day of the quarter regardless of signature date (we can accept a dated invoice to match Acme accounting).
- Replace monthly overage true-up with quarterly true-up and an automatic one-time credit if monthly usage stays within 5% of committed during Q1. That helps them avoid surprise charges.
- Offer a limited convert clause: if Acme expands beyond 150% of committed usage in a rolling quarter, they auto-qualify to a next-tier discount but must commit to additional prepay dollars (we’ll formalize the ladder).

I’ll draft the SKU mapping for the private-offer so the billing team can reconcile consumption to the AWS Marketplace SKU on their PO.

Marissa
Senior RevOps Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.inference.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.inference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Mon, 08 Nov 2026 12:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private Offer: annual prepay + ramp schedule — initial proposal (legal redline items)

Heads up — quick legal flags before we send anything customer-facing:

1) Termination for convenience: 30 days is OK but we should cap the refund admin fee at $5k or 1% of remaining prepay, whichever is lower. Avoid open-ended percentages.
2) Data residency / audit rights: confirm the exact AWS regions they expect. Add a clause about audit window (30 days notice) and we’ll provide SOC2/pen-test references rather than full raw reports without an NDA.
3) Liability/indemnity: limit liability to the amount paid under the prepay for the prior 12 months (if 24-month deal, cap to 12 months worth). That’s standard.

I’ve prepared a redline doc for the Private Offer (Redwood_PrivateOffer_Acme_2026_v1_redline.docx). Please confirm you’re happy to share this with Procurement as-is or if you want me to soften the admin fee language before external circulation.

Monica
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Redwood_PrivateOffer_Acme_2026_v1_redline.docx]

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.inference.com>
To: Alicia Gomez <agomez@acme-retail.com>, Ben Turner <b.turner@acme-retail.com>, Samir Desai <samir@aws-partner.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 08:15:00 -0800
Subject: Final: Acme private offer — Option A (annual prepay, smoother ramp) + DocuSign link

Alicia/Ben — thanks for the quick turnaround. Based on procurement and legal feedback we’re proceeding with Option A with the tweaks below. I’ve attached the private-offer PDF and the redline for transparency.

Final commercial summary (Option A - agreed):
- Term: 12 months, annual prepay $600k (invoice dated 11/30/2026 to align with Acme Q4 close)
- Ramp: M1=60%, M2=80%, M3+=100% availability
- Overages: up to 10% per month before automatic quarterly true-up; quarterly reconciliation and single true-up settlement
- Discount: 16% off list
- Termination: 30 days for convenience; admin fee capped at $5k or 1% of remaining prepay (we’ll set to $5k for this deal)
- Liability cap: amount paid in the prior 12 months

Attachments: Redwood_PrivateOffer_Acme_2026_v1.pdf, Redwood_PrivateOffer_Acme_2026_v1_redline.docx

Links: DocuSign offer (https://www.docusign.com/terms/abcd-1234-RDW-ACME) — please sign this to kick off the AWS private-offer flow. Samir — can you generate the AWS Private Offer link after DocuSign completes?

If you’d like, we can also prepare a 24-month Option B as an appendix to the offer for future renewal discussions — it would lock a deeper discount but requires a longer billing commitment.

Thanks all — aiming to have the private offer live in AWS Marketplace within 48 hours of DocuSign completion.

Best,
Sergio
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Redwood_PrivateOffer_Acme_2026_v1.pdf (final)]
